criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs plans a request about CI routing or parallel jobs against the real 2026-10-16 speed addendum text and asserts its rung is above Implementation. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: The test `a_request_serving_the_speed_addendum_ranks_above_implementation` loads the real BRIEF.md with include_str. It checks that the 2026-10-16 speed addendum is parsed with the text "intelligent routing". It then asserts that "Move compute to CI with intelligent routing of jobs" and "Run parallel jobs for initiatives" both get Some(BriefRequirements), which is less than Some(Implementation), meaning a higher rung. The test passed: 216 passed, 0 failed.

criteria.criterion: A unit test builds a plan from an old plain implementation request (a typo fix) and a newer speed-addendum request, and asserts the speed request is ordered first. Run `cargo test -p athena-core plan`.
criteria.evidence: The test `a_plan_orders_a_speed_request_before_an_older_typo_fix` builds `Plan::build(&[old_typo, new_speed])`, with the old item first in the input. It asserts that the old item's rung is Implementation and that the order is ["new", "old"]. The filtered run selected the test and it passed (12 passed).

criteria.criterion: A request that matches no brief section and has only an IMPLEMENTATION_WORDS word, such as 'fix a bug', no longer gets a rung from the word alone. A test asserts this, and the existing test `a_rung_is_inferred_from_evidence_or_flagged_never_defaulted_to_implementation` is updated to match.
criteria.evidence: The new test `a_word_like_fix_or_bug_alone_is_no_rung` uses the real brief and asserts None for "fix a bug", "fix the typo in the intro" and "update the docs and tests". The existing test now asserts None for "fix the typo in the intro" and "fix a bug", and Implementation for "fix the typo in README.md", which touches a path. Both tests passed. In the diff, the IMPLEMENTATION_WORDS branch is removed from `infer_rung`.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test` passes and `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean across the workspace.
criteria.evidence: Clippy with -D warnings finished with no warnings. `cargo test -q` reported "ok" for every test binary with 0 failed; the athena-core unit binary had 216 passed and 1 ignored.

criteria.criterion: The doc comments on `IMPLEMENTATION_WORDS`, `infer_rung` and the plan.rs module header say the rung comes from what a request serves in BRIEF.md and its addenda. A short entry in docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md records the call and the alternatives (a model-chosen rung, keeping the word list).
criteria.evidence: From the diff: the IMPLEMENTATION_WORDS doc says the words are "never a rung on their own: the rung comes from what the request serves in BRIEF.md and its addenda". The `infer_rung` doc opens with "found from what it serves in BRIEF.md and the owner's addenda". The plan.rs header says "the rung only from the caller or from what the request serves in BRIEF.md and its addenda". Decision D107 in docs/decisions.md lists both alternatives: (a) a model-chosen rung and (b) keeping the word list. The CHANGELOG Fixed entry names the root cause and both rejected alternatives.
The command printed nothing, so BRIEF.md has no diff.

findings.summary: One changed file, crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, is not on the expected deliverables list. The list names crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, which is unchanged.
findings.evidence: The diff stat shows crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs changed and no tests/drain.rs. The edit fills the new required `Lookup.brief` field at the only production call site of `plan_entry`, so the workspace would not compile without it. It is the wiring the reading's assumption calls for ("passed in through the Lookup struct"). The list most likely named the wrong file.

findings.summary: Rung matching ignores how recent an addendum is, and the two-word bar is low. Older requests that serve any addendum tie with the speed items at BriefRequirements, and age then orders them first.
findings.evidence: From the code: `serves_topic` accepts any of the roughly 25 addendum bodies under BRIEF.md `## Addenda` (lines 443-548), all treated the same, and maps every match to BriefRequirements. The request asks for ranking by "the owner's latest addenda". Many addendum bodies are long and use common project words such as job, role, decision, planning, parallel, track and state, so many older requests may also reach two shared words. D107 already notes this tradeoff. I did not measure the effect on the 30-item plan from #116, because records/ is absent from this snapshot. That the speed items will lead it is an estimate, not a result. A later refinement could weight the newest addenda.

findings.summary: No test covers the drain/plan CLI path that reads BRIEF.md at the base commit and passes it to `plan_entry`.
findings.evidence: The new behavior is tested only at the athena-core unit level with a brief passed in directly. The CLI wiring (`show_file(head, "BRIEF.md")` and `brief_topics`) is not exercised by any changed test, and crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs is unmodified.

findings.summary: Two edited doc lines are much longer than the lines around them, and one plan.rs sentence repeats "therefore".
findings.evidence: The plan.rs line "…whatever its age. A vague request such as \"make it better\" therefore has neither, is flagged" runs well past the wrap width of the nearby lines, and "therefore" now appears in two consecutive sentences. In roles-and-ladder.md, "(D107). Once a request is read, …" is likewise not rewrapped.

summary: The change does what the request and its accepted reading ask. `infer_rung` no longer treats a word like "fix", "code" or "ci" as evidence. A request that shares at least two significant words with a BRIEF.md requirement heading or an addendum (the BRIEF.md `###` sections that `brief_topics` reads) now ranks as BriefRequirements, above Implementation. The brief reaches `plan_entry` through `Lookup`, so planning does no I/O itself. The drain reads BRIEF.md at the base commit and passes it in. New tests run against the real BRIEF.md. They show that CI-routing and parallel-jobs requests rank above Implementation, that a newer speed request is planned before an older typo fix, and that "fix a bug" gets no rung. `cargo test`, `cargo test -p athena-core`, `cargo test -p athena-core plan` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` all passed when I ran them. BRIEF.md is unchanged, and the docs, decision D107 and the CHANGELOG entry are present. Four findings, none blocking: (1) one changed file, `crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs`, is not on the deliverables list. The list names `tests/drain.rs` instead, but the call site has to change for the code to compile. (2) The matching ignores how recent an addendum is, and two shared words is a low bar against about 25 long addenda. Older requests that touch any addendum will tie with the speed items, and age then puts them first. Whether the speed items actually lead the real 30-item plan was not measured here. (3) No CLI-level test covers the drain passing in BRIEF.md. (4) Two new doc lines are long and one sentence in plan.rs repeats "therefore".
